question: Should OpenClaw add a backend-neutral distributed scheduler/job ownership contract in core or plugin APIs, document Redis/BullMQ-style orchestration as external-only, or defer the broad queue layer to narrower cron/session/runtime trackers?
rationale: The missing capability is clear in source, but the backend boundary, config shape, credentials model, worker failure semantics, observability surface, and core-versus-plugin ownership require maintainer architecture intent.

options.title: Design backend-neutral contract
options.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, and observability before any Redis/BullMQ-specific code lands.

options.title: Document external pattern
options.body: Keep core single-process for now and document ScalyClaw/BullMQ-style orchestration as an external deployment or plugin pattern.

options.title: Defer to narrower trackers
options.body: Let cron HA, external session storage, and distributed runtime issues settle first, then revisit whether a broader worker layer is still needed.

recommendation.title: Design backend-neutral contract
recommendation.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, and observability before any Redis/BullMQ-specific code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current-main queue/cron history and already provided the prior architecture-review routing on this issue.
